results.raw_hits_note: Approximate count of postings individually keyword-matched and evaluated against the 3 filters, summed across the 3 parallel collection forks' per-source 'keyword hits of X reqs' figures. Several thousand more reqs were scanned in bulk at board-level (e.g. Stripe 717, Cloudflare 451, Datadog 426, Elastic 402, Okta 389, Zscaler 350, Crusoe 349, Palantir 309, Canonical 314, GitLab 239, Wiz 123, Leidos ~109 matched, Octopus/Kraken 173, Hut8 47) without every individual JD being opened, so this figure undercounts true board-level scan volume.
results.collection_method_note: Three collection forks ran in parallel this run, each scoped to a disjoint slice of resources/sources.md to avoid the duplication problem noted in the 2026-10-19 log: (1) cloud-native tech + Seattle-area majors, (2) energy-sector + Palantir/Leidos, (3) newly-formalized/new-ATS/promising-leads/aggregators + LinkedIn. Each fork was instructed to do its own Step 3.5 live-URL validation inline and not to write any files or commit; the orchestrating main thread compiled, curated for redundancy, wrote the report/log, updated resources/sources.md, and committed.

token_usage.note: Exact figures for all 3 collection forks, taken directly from their completion notifications. Main-thread usage is not measurable precisely for this run; proxy below.

main_thread_tool_calls_estimate.note: Main thread (orchestrator) did not independently fetch any job URLs or APIs this run — all collection, filtering, and Step 3.5 validation was performed by the 3 forks above; main thread only read sources.md/workflow/prior logs, compiled/curated the 17 qualifying roles to 14, wrote the report/log, edited resources/sources.md, and handled the dashboard update and commit.

timing.step3_3.5_filter_and_validation_minutes_: done inline during collection by each fork, not separately timed
timing.step6_top_pick_spotcheck_minutes_approx: covered inline during collection (ATS JSON API re-validation performed at collection time for top picks)
timing.note: step2 wall-clock time approximated from the longest-running fork's duration_ms (~405s); the 3 forks ran concurrently rather than sequentially, so this is far less than the sum of their individual durations.
